questions.question: A display is running at 90 Hz. What is the display interval before reserving time for runtime and compositor work?
options: About 11.1 ms
About 90 ms
About 20 ms
Exactly 8.3 ms
questions.explanation: The interval is 1000 / 90, or about 11.1 ms. The application usually owns less than the full interval.

questions.question: Why should one frame use a consistent predicted display time across tracking, simulation, and view location?
options: To avoid different subsystems describing the world at incompatible times
To make network round trips disappear
To guarantee every device uses 120 Hz
To turn spatial anchors into an authority service
questions.explanation: A consistent target time keeps motion, simulation, and rendered views temporally coherent and reduces judder-producing disagreement.

questions.question: A GPU-heavy scene starts missing its frame deadline. Which response best protects the core experience?
options: Reduce render scale or optional visual work before weakening tracking, input, or safety
Delay all head-pose updates until the backend responds
Increase every texture resolution
Disable the user's exit path
questions.explanation: Optional fidelity is the safer degradation lever. Tracking, control, safety, and clear recovery must remain coherent.

questions.question: What does a shared spatial anchor provide?
options: A common spatial relationship for placing content
Exclusive object ownership
Durable command ordering
Automatic duplicate suppression
questions.explanation: Anchors align content with a tracked location. Ownership, authorization, ordering, and durable state require separate application contracts.

questions.question: Which authority path best fits high-rate head and hand pose updates?
options: Render locally and send disposable samples for remote interpolation
Wait for a durable database commit before every local pose
Require an exclusive ownership transfer for every sample
Store every pose forever
questions.explanation: Local pose must remain immediate. Remote representations can consume recent samples and discard stale ones because pose is transient state.

questions.question: What must happen when an anticipated shared action loses to the authoritative result?
options: The client reconciles its visual state and makes consequential correction visible
Both results remain authoritative
The server accepts the client's value unconditionally
The client hides the disagreement forever
questions.explanation: Anticipation improves responsiveness but does not replace authority. Reconciliation restores one accepted state when the prediction is wrong.
